title: Source-degenerated CS amp
description: A common-source stage with a source-degeneration resistor $R_s$. The degeneration lowers the effective transconductance to $G_m = g_m/(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$ and raises the device output resistance by the same factor, so into an ideal load the intrinsic gain is unchanged; the payoff is linearity, since the stage transconductance is set by the (linear) resistor rather than the (nonlinear) device $g_m$. The cost is $R_s$'s own $4kT*R_s$ thermal noise, added directly at the input. The device source sits $I_{bias}*R_s$ above ground, so the bind declares $V_{SB} = I_{bias}*R_s$ (body grounded) — and the resistor degenerates the source-body generator $g_{mb}$ along with $g_m$, since both currents flow through it. A table that carries no $g_{mb}$ column leaves the gain rows unresolved rather than quietly dropping the term. Sweep $R_s$ to trade gain and noise against linearity.

params.name: V_out
params.note: drain DC level; the device vds is this minus the degenerated source level

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistance presented to the stage output

params.name: R_s
params.note: degeneration resistor: larger R_s linearizes the stage (Gm -> 1/R_s) but lowers gain and adds 4kT*R_s noise

rows.name: loop
rows.note: degeneration factor: how far gm is traded for linearity and raised output resistance. The source-body generator sees the same resistor as gm, so it degenerates with it — the gmb term adds about a fifth on top of the gm term, and dropping it overstates the gain by roughly 7% on a sky130 tt realization of this stage (about 6% on the demo table)

rows.name: Gm
rows.note: degenerated transconductance; approaches 1/R_s (resistor-set, linear) for (gm + gmb)*R_s >> 1

rows.name: Rout_dev
rows.note: degeneration boosts the device output resistance by the same factor Gm is lowered

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the load resistor in parallel with the degeneration-boosted device resistance. The load knob is already inside this row and inside the gain, so the loading contract here is the arithmetic rather than a separate rule

rows.name: Av
rows.note: degenerated transconductance into the load; into an ideal load Av -> gm/gds (gain preserved, linearity gained)

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: channel noise is unchanged input-referred; the degeneration resistor adds 4kT*R_s directly at the input

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents — this stage's gate capacitance. The table carries the TOTAL gate capacitance with no gate-drain split, so nothing here can weight the two terminals by how much each one swings: the inverting drain would multiply its share, while the degenerated source follows PART of the gate swing — the fraction 1 - 1/loop, about a third at these defaults — and bootstraps that much of $C_{GS}$ away. The two corrections pull opposite ways and neither is computable from this data. No rule reads it

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
device saturated: the drain-to-source voltage is the drain level minus the I*R_s source lift
computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
